text.p: These are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN

- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, addressing foreign ministers of Islamic countries in New York, called upon the international community to fulfil its obligations towards the suffering people of Kashmir without concern for the political or commercial expediency.
- The Karachi Electric Supply Corporation on Wednesday announced a 50 percent rise in service connection charges and security deposits on new connections.

- The Ministry of Justice has made a formal request to the Supreme Court to nominate a judge to preside over the tribunal that will investigate the killing of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza Bhutto.

- Pakistani officials' talks with the International Monetary Fund in Washington are progressing well and "we hope to achieve our goal", Minister of State for Finance Makhdoom Shahabuddin told reporters there on Wednesday.
THE NEWS

- U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said at a meeting with Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto in New York on Wednesday that United Nations owed $60 million to Pakistan for the country's formidable contribution towards U.N. peace-keeping operations.

- Chief of the Army Staff General Jehangir Karamat met President Farooq Leghari in Islamabad on Wednesday, briefed him on external and internal scenarios and discussed recent developments in the context of Afghanistan and eastern borders with India.

- Jamaat-i-Islami party chief Qazi Hussain Ahmad told a news conference in Islamabad on Wednesday that his party would stage a sit-in in the capital on October 24 to protest against alleged government corruption.
THE NATION

- A three-member bench of the Supreme Court will begin the hearing of a reference from President Farooq Leghari to interpret the constitutional provisions regarding his powers to appoint judges of superior courts.

- The Indian attempt to change the status of the "working boundary" between Pakistan's Punjab province and Indian-held Kashmir is creating trouble in Sialkot sector as border security forces of both countries are engtangled in a continuous crossfire for the last four days.
THE MUSLIM

- Minister of State for Law and Parliamentary Affairs Raza Rabbani assured the Senate (upper house) on Wednesday that Pakistan would not sign the Comprehensive (nuclear) Test Ban Treaty unless India does the same.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- A latest comparative study by the State (central) Bank of Pakistan shows that the amount of bad debts or stuck up loans in the banking system has shot up to 52 billion rupees from 24 billion within the last two years.
- Pakistan is likely to give the most favoured nation status to India by the end of October, sources said.
- Commerce Minister Ahmed Mukhtar said the government will allow free trade of sugar next year to make sugar industry more competitive.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
